## What's new

**Updating promptly is recommended.** This release closes weaknesses in the
update process on self-hosted installations.

### Fixed

- **Several gaps have been closed in how the application's own files are owned
  and protected during an update.** On a server running the application, it was
  possible for the unprivileged account the application runs under to obtain
  more access than it should have. The boundary that account is meant to be
  confined to now holds throughout an update, including for the files the
  updater itself reads and restores from.

- **The update process no longer trusts a stored configuration value when
  deciding where to fetch updates from.** The update source is verified before
  it is used, rather than assumed.

### Changed

- **Updates now stop with a clear message instead of continuing** if the
  configured access token is not a well-formed GitHub token, or if the
  repository the installation updates from is not on github.com. Standard
  installations are unaffected — this only surfaces where one of those values
  was already wrong or unusual. Using a self-hosted mirror as the update source
  is no longer supported; such installations could not receive update
  notifications in any case.

Existing installations pick this up automatically on their next scheduled
update. No configuration change is required, and no action is needed beyond
updating.
